gaps.sentence: The meeting has been ___ forward to Monday.
gaps.explanation: 'bring forward' = move to an earlier time (opposite of put off).

gaps.sentence: I'd like to know when the results ___ be published.
gaps.explanation: Future in a noun clause: when the results will be published.

gaps.sentence: We ran out ___ petrol on the motorway.
gaps.explanation: 'run out OF something' = have none left.

gaps.sentence: She speaks English ___ than her brother.
She's very good ___ explaining difficult ideas.
It was ___ a lovely evening that nobody wanted to leave.
gaps.explanation: 'Such a lovely evening that …' — 'so' would go directly before an adjective.

gaps.sentence: I'm not used to ___ such spicy food.
